channel.title: Dev|Journal
channel.description: Technical blog covering software architecture, backend development, and AI.

item.title: Your API Doesn't Need Versioning
item.description: The default approach to API design is to prefix routes with version numbers like /api/v1/ and /api/v2/. In practice, route versioning leads to massive code duplication, client migration paralysis, and complex routing tables. Designing backward-compatible APIs is a much better operational model.

item.title: Why We Should Stop Writing 'Smart' Code
item.description: Writing clever, concise, one-liner code is a common developer ego trip. In practice, 'smart' code is a maintenance liability that increases cognitive load, slows down debugging, and confuses your colleagues. Readable code is boring, obvious, and explicit.

item.title: Inheritance is a Relic: Composition Over Class Hierarchies
item.description: Object-oriented programming taught us that code reuse is achieved through class inheritance. In practice, deep inheritance hierarchies create fragile base classes, high coupling, and rigid domain structures. It is time to abandon inheritance and embrace composition.

item.title: No, You Don't Need a Service Mesh
item.description: Service meshes like Istio or Linkerd promise advanced traffic management, mutual TLS, and observability for microservices. In reality, they add massive networking complexity, consume significant CPU and RAM, and make debugging network issues a nightmare. Keep your cluster networking simple.

item.title: Why MongoDB is Still the Wrong Choice for 99% of Projects
item.description: The 'schemaless' pitch of document databases promised database flexibility and rapid iteration. In reality, your data always has schema. Moving schema constraints to the application layer leads to data drift, write corruption, and slow queries. PostgreSQL is almost always the correct answer.

item.title: The Fallacy of DRY: Why You Should Write Duplicated Code First
item.description: Don't Repeat Yourself (DRY) is one of the first design principles programmers learn. But applying it too early creates tightly coupled, hyper-flexible abstractions that crumble under the weight of changing requirements. Write duplicated code until the structure reveals itself.

item.title: Your Unit Tests Are Mocking You
item.description: Unit testing with mocked dependencies has become a software industry obsession. We write tests that verify our code behaves against mock assumptions, resulting in green test suites that pass while production crashes. It is time to embrace integration tests with real, lightweight dependencies.

item.title: Serverless is a Scam (and the Cloud Providers Know It)
item.description: Serverless computing promised to eliminate server management and lower costs by charging only for actual execution time. Instead, it delivered vendor lock-in, cold-start latency, database connection bottlenecks, and sky-high bills for consistent traffic workloads. A standard VPS remains the pragmatic choice.

item.title: Why Python is the Worst Language to Teach Beginners
item.description: Python has become the default first language in universities and bootcamps. But its magical syntax, lack of explicit types, hidden memory models, and chaotic package ecosystem teach beginners terrible habits and make transitioning to other languages unnecessarily painful.

item.title: The CSS-in-JS Fever Dream is Over
item.description: For years, frontend developers insisted that CSS should be written in JavaScript. We got dynamic styling at the cost of massive runtime overhead, bloated bundle sizes, and broken browser style injection. Now, the fever dream is over. Tailwind and modern CSS features have won.

item.title: Your Local Development Environment Should Not Run on Docker
item.description: Docker is an excellent tool for production deployments, but running your entire local development environment in containers is a productivity killer. It slows down tests, eats memory, complicates debugging, and isolates developers from the tools they need. Let's make local development native again.

item.title: Why Clean Architecture is a Maintainability Nightmare
item.description: Robert C. Martin's 'Clean Architecture' promises to decouple your business logic from external frameworks and databases. In practice, it leads to a sprawling wasteland of boilerplate, interface layers that pass data straight through, and excessive mapping functions. Here's why YAGNI should trump architecture dogmatism.

item.title: Codexity Part 8: The Complete Answer Engine
item.description: The final chapter. Assemble every module into a running application. Complete source code, Docker deployment, configuration, testing, and performance tuning for the full Codexity answer engine.

item.title: Agile is Dead, and Scrum Murdered It
item.description: The Agile Manifesto was a beautiful statement of developer autonomy and adaptive planning. Scrum turned it into an oppressive, ceremony-heavy micromanagement machine. Here's how story points, standups, and retrospectives killed the spirit of software engineering.

item.title: Codexity Part 7: Server-Sent Events and Streaming
item.description: Implement production-grade SSE streaming in FastAPI. Handle connection drops, heartbeats, backpressure, error recovery, and the HTTP details that make streaming reliable.

item.title: Rust is Great, but You're Probably Using it for the Wrong Reasons
item.description: Rust is the darling of the systems programming world, boasting safety and performance without a garbage collector. But rewriting your company's simple HTTP CRUD API in Rust is likely a waste of time and money. Here is why the productivity hit of Rust is rarely worth it for typical web applications.

item.title: The TypeScript Tax: When Type Safety Becomes a Development Bottleneck
item.description: TypeScript has become the default choice for JS development, and for good reason. But the pendulum has swung too far. Developers are spending hours writing complex generic wizardry, mapping types, and fighting compiler warnings instead of shipping features. Here's a look at the hidden costs of type pedantry.

item.title: Codexity Part 6: Small Model Inference with llama-cpp-python
item.description: Run a quantized 7B model locally to generate cited answers from scraped web content. Choose between Qwen, Mistral, Phi, and Llama models. Build prompts that make small models behave like large ones.

item.title: Why ORMs are the Worst Anti-Pattern in Modern Backend Development
item.description: Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) tools promise to free developers from SQL. In exchange, they introduce the N+1 query problem, hide database performance realities behind black-box abstractions, and create models that couple application state to database schemas. It's time to write SQL again.

item.title: Codexity Part 5: Content Processing and Relevance Ranking
item.description: Take raw scraped text from 12 web pages and transform it into a focused context window for an LLM. Chunk text, score relevance with BM25, select the best fragments, and format them with source citations.

item.title: The Lie of 'No-Code' and Why AI Won't Replace Programmers
item.description: With the rise of LLMs, pundits are declaring the 'end of coding.' But this view fundamentally misunderstands what programming actually is. Writing syntax is the easy part; the hard part is translating ambiguous human desires into rigorous, deterministic logic. AI is an accelerator, not a replacement.

item.title: Microservices: The Great Architecture Grift of the 2010s
item.description: The industry fell head-over-heels for microservices, believing they would solve all development bottlenecks. Instead, we traded in-process function calls for unreliable network requests, simple joins for distributed transactions, and single deployments for orchestration nightmares. The monolith was right all along.

item.title: Codexity Part 4: Web Scraping, Proxies, and Anti-Bot Warfare
item.description: Fetch and extract content from 15 web pages concurrently. Handle JavaScript rendering with Playwright, dodge anti-bot systems, rotate proxies, and strip HTML down to clean text using readability-lxml and BeautifulSoup.

item.description: A solo operator uses five primitives—browser agents, coding agents, schedules, memory, and gates—to replace 2-4 full-time roles for a few hundred dollars monthly.

item.description: Explore lossless compression strategies—like deduplication and entity extraction—to reduce token usage by up to 50% in RAG pipelines.

item.description: A rollback endpoint accepted a deployment ID in the URL path and ignored it, always restoring the most recent version instead of the one requested.

item.title: Binary Search Over a Rank Oracle Turns a Skewed Crawl from One Week to One Day
item.description: A single shard held 71% of the work in a 4M-item crawl. A binary search over an offset oracle balanced partitions and cut finish time from one week to one day.

item.description: Three Sui protocols lost $224M+ to arithmetic bugs that audits missed — the same root cause: incomplete boundary checks.
